figures.caption: **Figure 1. Three ways to get data abroad.** They differ in how you pay (the green row), whether you get a number, and what your phone needs.
figures.alt: Three ways to get data abroad

figures.caption: **Figure 2. Two ways to carry the same key.** A card and an eSIM reach the same towers. Neither one is a different network.
figures.alt: Figure 2. Two ways to carry the same key. A card and an eSIM reach the same towers. Neither one is a different network.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. A locked phone won't take a travel eSIM or a local SIM.** On an iPhone, the Carrier Lock line tells you. “No SIM restrictions” means it's unlocked.
**Figure 4. No SIM tray means eSIM only.** Many new phones have no slot. A SIM card from an airport kiosk won't fit, so buy an eSIM instead.
figures.alt: A phone with no SIM tray takes eSIMs only

figures.caption: **Figure 5. Three roads to the same towers.** Each one bills you differently.
figures.alt: Figure 5. Three roads to the same towers. Each one bills you differently.

figures.caption: **Figure 6. A daily fee adds up.** On a trip of over a week, a monthly travel plan usually costs less than paying by the day.
figures.alt: Figure 6. A daily fee adds up. On a trip of over a week, a monthly travel plan usually costs less than paying by the day.

figures.caption: **Figure 7. A travel eSIM in three steps.** Set it up at home, switch it on when you land, and switch it off when you're back.
figures.alt: Figure 7. A travel eSIM in three steps. Set it up at home, switch it on when you land, and switch it off when you're back.

figures.caption: **Figure 8. One phone, two plans, two jobs.** Your home plan takes calls and texts. The travel plan carries the data.
figures.alt: Figure 8. One phone, two plans, two jobs. Your home plan takes calls and texts. The travel plan carries the data.

figures.caption: **Figure 9. Your home line still rings abroad.** Data Roaming off doesn't stop any of these.

**Figure 10. Which switch stops what.** Data Roaming off stops data, but calls and texts still get through, and can still cost you. With Wi-Fi Calling on, calls and texts still work over Wi-Fi, even in airplane mode.
**Figure 11. The sign-in page stands between the Wi-Fi and the internet.** Full Wi-Fi bars only mean step 1 worked. Nothing else loads until you sign in.
**Figure 12. A starting point, not a rule.** For a trip of over a week, a monthly plan usually beats paying by the day.
figures.alt: Figure 12. A starting point, not a rule. For a trip of over a week, a monthly plan usually beats paying by the day.

figures.caption: **Figure 13. Your trip, in four stops.** Two small jobs at each one. The green stop, when you land, is where the switches matter.
figures.alt: Your trip checklist as a timeline
